---
title: 'flora_species_gap'
description: 'Find species that occur in Brazil but are missing from FFB'
toc: true
toc-depth: 3
---


```{r}
#| eval: false
floraR::flora_species_gap()
```

### Description

Given one or more genera of plants or algae, finds the species-level names that global sources
record for Brazil but that are not currently registered in the Flora e Funga do
Brasil (FFB) - candidates for inclusion in the FFB monograph of the group. Two
independent kinds of evidence, from up to four sources, are combined (see
`sources`):

- **POWO distributions**: species that [Plants of the World Online](https://powo.science.kew.org) (POWO, Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew) maps in Brazil;
- **Type specimens**: species whose type specimens - holotypes, isotypes, lectotypes, syntypes, paratypes, and so on - were collected in Brazil, according to the herbaria that publish them through the [Global Biodiversity Information Facility](https://www.gbif.org) (GBIF), the [Reflora Virtual Herbarium](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/reflora/herbarioVirtual/), and [JABOT](https://jabot.jbrj.gov.br).

The result is a single table, one row per name, stating which source(s) reported it:
the more sources report a name, the stronger the candidate, and combining them
retrieves as many gaps as possible. This is not a general diff of
the databases: a name missing from FFB is only returned when there is evidence that
the species occurs in Brazil.

### Details

**FFB side.** Names are compared against the locally cached FFB dataset (as in
`flora_download` and `flora_parse`). A name counts as
"already in FFB" if either the name itself or its *accepted* name (in POWO or
GBIF) matches any FFB name - accepted or synonym, anywhere in the checklist, since
checklists disagree on generic placement (e.g. a *Myrcia* synonym accepted as
*Eugenia florida*). Names are compared ignoring case, diacritics, hyphens,
*y*/*i*, and the genitive *-ii*/*-i* ending, so orthographic variants such as
*Luetzelburgia andrade-limae* and FFB's *L. andradelimae* are not
reported. Only species-level names are reported.

**POWO** (`"powo"`). POWO's names, synonymy, and distribution maps come
from the [World Checklist of Vascular
Plants](https://powo.science.kew.org/about-wcvp) (WCVP), read from one of two sources chosen with `powo_source`:

- `"rWCVPdata"` (default): The whole WCVP, installed locally by the [rWCVPdata](https://github.com/matildabrown/rWCVPdata) package: every name and distribution of the genus is resolved at once, in memory. The data is as current as the installed release (see `rWCVPdata::wcvp_check_version()`). rWCVPdata is not on CRAN; install it with `install.packages("rWCVPdata", repos = c("https://matildabrown.github.io/drat", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))`.
- `"checklistbank"`: POWO's own weekly export and WCVP, as hosted on [ChecklistBank](https://www.checklistbank.org) (POWO's own API blocks programmatic clients). Always current and needs no extra package, but slower: one request per FFB-missing name.

A POWO name has Brazil evidence when its accepted name occurs in at least one of the
five TDWG level-3 areas covering Brazil - Brazil North (`BZN`), Northeast
(`BZE`), West-Central (`BZC`), Southeast (`BZL`), and South
(`BZS`); native, introduced, or extinct, but not doubtful. Without a mapped
distribution, POWO's free-text range (e.g. `"Brazil (Bahia)"`) is checked
instead. POWO covers vascular plants only, so it finds nothing for algae.

**GBIF** (`"gbif"`). The genus is looked up among plants and algae only -
the GBIF kingdoms Plantae (land plants, red and green algae), Chromista (brown algae,
diatoms), and Protozoa (euglenids) - so a genus name shared with an animal (e.g.
*Gracilaria*, both a red alga and a moth) resolves to the plant or alga. A
single faceted search lists every name in the genus with type specimens collected in
Brazil; for the FFB-missing names only, the specimens themselves are then retrieved,
many names per request, and summarised. Types are filed in GBIF under their current
identification - usually the typified name - which `GBIF_Specimen_names` shows.

**REFLORA** (`"reflora"`) and **JABOT** (`"jabot"`). The
specimens of the genus are read with `reflora_records` and
`jabot_records` (requiring the refloraR and jabotR
packages), from their herbaria's Darwin Core archives: the first use downloads them -
several gigabytes - to `"reflora_download"` and `"jabot_download"` in the
working directory, where they are reused by later calls. Reading them takes a few
minutes, so they are read only once per call, for all the genera in `taxon`
together: checking many genera in one call is much faster than one call per
genus. The species-level names of the specimens collected in
Brazil that are types (any type status) are compared with FFB; as in GBIF, a
specimen is filed under its current identification. Use `sources = c("powo",
"gbif")` for a quick check.

In all three specimen sources, type statuses are standardised with
`barRoso::std_types()` (e.g. `"HOLOTYPUS"` and `"Holotype"` both
become `"holotype"`) and places with `barRoso::std_place()`.

**Several genera.** Each genus in `taxon` is analysed separately, and its
spreadsheet and HTML report are saved under its own name,
`flora_species_gap_<genus>` (e.g. `flora_species_gap_Myrcia.xlsx`). A
genus that fails (e.g. a misspelt name) is reported and skipped, without stopping
the others.

**Genera with nothing missing.** A genus without any species missing from FFB
needs no FFB update, so no spreadsheet or detailed report is written for it.
Instead, all such genera of a call are listed in a single, simple HTML report,
`<dir>/__no_missing_species_report.html` (written when `html_report =
TRUE`), with what was searched for each - its number of species in FFB and of names
with evidence in each source - and a conclusion: `"All names already in FFB -
no update needed"`, or `"No names found - check the genus"` when the sources
returned nothing at all.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| taxon | Character vector. One or more genus names of plants or algae (e.g. `"Myrcia"`, `"Gracilaria"`, or `c("Myrcia", "Eugenia")`). Each is analysed separately; see Details. Fungi are not searched. |
| sources | Character vector. Which sources of evidence to use: any of `"powo"` (POWO distributions), `"gbif"`, `"reflora"`, and `"jabot"` (Brazilian type specimens in GBIF, REFLORA, and JABOT). Defaults to all four, combining their evidence; see Details for the requirements of each. |
| keep_downloads | Logical. Applies to REFLORA and JABOT. If `TRUE` (default), the herbarium archives downloaded to `"reflora_download"` and `"jabot_download"` in the working directory are kept, so that later runs - for this or other taxa - reuse them instead of downloading them again. If `FALSE`, those folders are deleted once the analysis is finished, leaving the working directory clean (they take several gigabytes). |
| powo_source | Character. Where POWO's data is read from: `"rWCVPdata"` (default; fast, local) or `"checklistbank"` (always current, slower). See Details. |
| require_brazil_evidence | Logical. Applies to POWO. If `TRUE` (default), POWO names are only kept when POWO places the species in Brazil. Set to `FALSE` to also return POWO names missing from FFB regardless of distribution, for manual review. (Names from the specimen sources always have Brazil evidence: their types were collected there.) |
| type_status | Character or `NULL`. Applies to GBIF. Type statuses counted as evidence (GBIF's current vocabulary, e.g. `"Holotype"`, `"Isotype"`). `NULL` (default) uses all primary and secondary type categories: Type, Holotype, Isotype, Lectotype, Isolectotype, Syntype, Isosyntype, Neotype, Isoneotype, Epitype, Isoepitype, Paratype, Isoparatype, Paralectotype, OriginalMaterial, and TypeSeries. |
| fetch_details | Logical. Applies to POWO with `powo_source = "checklistbank"`: if `TRUE` (default), each candidate's protologue citation is fetched (one request per name). With `"rWCVPdata"` it is always included. |
| max_number | Numeric. Applies to POWO with `powo_source = "checklistbank"`: maximum number of names retrieved. Defaults to `5000`. |
| version | Character. FFB dataset version to compare against. Defaults to `"latest"`. Passed to `flora_download`. |
| verbose | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints progress messages. |
| save | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), the result of each genus with at least one species missing from FFB is saved to disk as an `.xlsx` spreadsheet named after the genus, `flora_species_gap_<genus>.xlsx`. Genera with nothing missing get no spreadsheet (see Details). |
| dir | Character. Directory where the spreadsheets and reports are saved. Defaults to `"flora_species_gap"`. |
| html_report | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), also writes a self-contained HTML report for each genus with missing species (`<dir>/flora_species_gap_<genus>.html`), plus a single `<dir>/__no_missing_species_report.html` listing the genera with nothing missing (see Details) summarizing the results: KPI counts and the full candidate table as a sortable, filterable DT widget with buttons to copy or download it as CSV/Excel. Requires the rmarkdown, DT, and htmltools packages; if any is missing, the report is skipped with a message (the `.xlsx` spreadsheet is unaffected). |
| open_report | Logical. If `TRUE`, opens the HTML report in the browser once rendered (in interactive sessions only). Default `FALSE`: the report is only saved to `dir`. |

### Value

A `data.frame`, one row per species-level name in the genus (or
  genera, stacked one after the other) that is absent from the current FFB checklist and reported by at least one source, sorted
  with the names reported by more sources first. Common columns:

- Taxon_name, Authors: The name and its author citation.
- Accepted_name: The accepted name (POWO's when available, else GBIF's; for names only in REFLORA or JABOT, the name itself).
- Found_in: Which source(s) reported the name, e.g. `"POWO; GBIF; REFLORA"`, `"GBIF; JABOT"`, or `"POWO"`.
- Brazil_evidence: Logical; `TRUE` when POWO places the species in Brazil or it has Brazilian type specimens in GBIF, REFLORA, or JABOT.
- In_FFB: Always `FALSE` (kept for clarity when combining with other tables).

POWO columns (when `"powo"` is among `sources`; `NA` for names POWO
did not report):

- POWO_ID, POWO_Taxonomic_status, POWO_Accepted_name: The name's POWO (IPNI) identifier, status (e.g. `"Accepted"`, `"Synonym"`), and accepted name.
- POWO_Year, POWO_Published_in: Year of publication and protologue citation.
- POWO_Range: POWO's free-text range.
- POWO_Distribution, POWO_Brazil_Areas: Every TDWG level-3 area of the accepted name's distribution, and only the Brazilian ones.
- POWO_Brazil_Evidence, POWO_Evidence_Source: Whether POWO places the species in Brazil, and whether from the `"WCVP distribution"` or the `"POWO range text"`.
- POWO_URL, IPNI_URL: Links to the name's POWO and IPNI pages.

GBIF columns (when `"gbif"` is among `sources`; `NA` for names GBIF
did not report):

- GBIF_Key, GBIF_Taxonomic_status, GBIF_Accepted_name: The name's GBIF backbone key, status (e.g. `"ACCEPTED"`, `"DOUBTFUL"`), and accepted species.
- GBIF_N_type_specimens, GBIF_Type_statuses: Number of type specimens collected in Brazil, and their type categories.
- GBIF_Type_specimens: Up to ten specimens as herbarium, catalogue number, and type status (e.g. `"RB 00123 (holotype)"`).
- GBIF_Specimen_names: The names the types are filed under - usually the typified name, e.g. the basionym of a species.
- GBIF_Collectors, GBIF_Years, GBIF_States: Collectors, collection years, and Brazilian states of those specimens.
- GBIF_Published_in, GBIF_URL: Protologue citation, when GBIF has it, and a link to the name's GBIF page.

REFLORA and JABOT columns (when `"reflora"` or `"jabot"` is among
`sources`), prefixed `REFLORA_` or `JABOT_`:

- N_type_specimens, Type_statuses, Type_specimens: Number of type specimens collected in Brazil, their type categories, and up to ten of them as herbarium, catalogue number, and type status.
- Collectors, Years, States: Collectors, collection years, and Brazilian states of those specimens.
- Links: Up to three links to the specimens' pages (REFLORA only; JABOT records carry no link).

### Examples

```r
# Species of Myrcia recorded in Brazil by POWO and/or with Brazilian type
# specimens in GBIF, REFLORA, or JABOT, but missing from FFB
gap <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia")

# A quick check, without the REFLORA and JABOT archives
gap_quick <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", sources = c("powo", "gbif"))

# Several genera in one call: REFLORA and JABOT are read once, and each genus
# gets its own spreadsheet and report
gap_many <- flora_species_gap(taxon = c("Myrcia", "Eugenia", "Calyptranthes"))

# POWO only, read live from ChecklistBank instead of the local WCVP copy
gap_powo <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", sources = "powo",
                              powo_source = "checklistbank")

# An algal genus: GBIF type specimens only (POWO covers vascular plants)
gap_algae <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Gracilaria", sources = "gbif")

# Stricter type evidence: holotypes and isotypes only
gap_strict <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia",
                                type_status = c("Holotype", "Isotype"))
```
